pack.name: EU AI Act — core qualification
pack.source_version: Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 as amended by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744, Official Journal texts

application_timeline.event: Chapters I and II apply, including Articles 4 and 5
General application date, subject to Article 113 exceptions
Chapter III Sections 1 to 3 apply to Article 6(2) and Annex III high-risk systems
Chapter III Sections 1 to 3 apply to Article 6(1) and Annex I high-risk systems

coverage: high-risk qualification entry points under Article 6 and Annex III employment uses
AI literacy under Article 4 as amended in 2026
known_gaps: This is a triage core, not an exhaustive conformity checklist.
Most Annex III areas are not yet encoded beyond employment and worker management.
Annex I product legislation requires a sector-specific profile.
The Article 5 prohibitions added by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 are disclosed in the source timeline but not yet encoded as rules.
GPAI model obligations, notified bodies, market surveillance and penalties are not yet encoded.
Commission guidelines, harmonised standards and delegated amendments require separate reviewed releases.
pack.notice: A matched result is a legal triage signal, not a certification or legal opinion. Verify facts, current law and applicable guidance.

fact_catalog.question: Does the composition meet the Regulation's AI-system definition?
In which domain is the system intended to be used?
Which material tasks form the intended purpose?
Which Annex III use case, if any, applies?
Does the system profile natural persons within Article 6(3)?
Does the system pose a significant risk of harm to health, safety or fundamental rights?
Does the system materially influence the outcome of decision-making?
Is the system intended to perform a narrow procedural task?
Is it intended to improve the result of a previously completed human activity?
Does it detect decision-making patterns or deviations without being meant to replace or influence a previously completed human assessment without proper human review?
Is it intended to perform a preparatory task to an assessment relevant to an Annex III use?
Does the system infer emotions?
Is the emotion inference intended for medical or safety reasons?
Does the system deploy prohibited manipulative, subliminal or deceptive techniques?
Does it materially distort informed decision-making?
Does it cause or reasonably likely cause significant harm?
Does the system meet the amended Article 3(14) safety-component definition, including the Article 6(1a) and 6(1b) clarifications?
Does Annex I legislation require third-party conformity assessment?
Is third-party conformity assessment required solely for non-health-and-safety risks within Article 6(1c)?
Has a distributor, importer, deployer or other third party put its name or trademark on an existing high-risk AI system?
Has an actor substantially modified an existing high-risk AI system in a way that leaves it high-risk?
Did an actor change the intended purpose so the system becomes high-risk?
Is the system intended to interact directly with natural persons?
Is the AI nature obvious to a reasonably informed, observant and circumspect person?
Is the system authorised by law for criminal-offence detection, prevention, investigation or prosecution and covered by the Article 50(1) exception?
Does the organisation provide or deploy AI systems?
Are measures in place to support development of AI literacy for relevant staff and other persons operating or using AI on the organisation's behalf?
Do instructions or capabilities support analysing, filtering or ranking applications?

anchors.summary: Definitions, including AI system, intended purpose, provider, deployer and substantial modification.
Providers and deployers must take measures to support development of AI literacy; they do not have to guarantee a specific level for any individual.
Selected prohibited practices, including harmful manipulation and emotion inference in workplaces or education subject to limited exceptions.
High-risk classification for Annex I products and Annex III uses, including the narrow Article 6(3) exception.
Clarifies safety components and excludes third-party assessment triggered solely by specified non-health-and-safety risks from the Article 6(1) route.
Sets 2 December 2027 for Chapter III Sections 1 to 3 for Annex III systems and 2 August 2028 for Annex I systems.
Employment and worker-management systems, including targeted recruitment advertising, analysis and filtering of applications, candidate evaluation and certain employment decisions.
Certain distributors, importers, deployers or third parties become providers when they rebrand, substantially modify or change the intended purpose of a high-risk system.
Providers of systems intended to interact directly with people must generally inform them that they are interacting with AI.

finding.title: The described practice matches a prohibited-practice pattern
finding.summary: The supplied facts indicate manipulative, subliminal or deceptive techniques that materially distort decisions and cause or are reasonably likely to cause significant harm.

reason.matched: All three cumulative triage facts are established.
reason.indeterminate: At least one cumulative legal element is missing or conflicted.
reason.not_matched: At least one cumulative element is not established.

obligations.title: Do not place, put into service or use the practice without immediate specialist review.

rules.title: Emotion inference in workplace or education

finding.title: Emotion inference falls within the workplace or education prohibition
finding.summary: The use infers emotions in a workplace or education context and no medical or safety exception is established.

obligations.title: Stop the proposed practice and obtain specialist review.

finding.title: The system matches the Article 6(1) product route
finding.summary: It is a safety component or covered product, the relevant Annex I legislation requires third-party conformity assessment, and that assessment is not required solely for a non-health-and-safety risk excluded by Article 6(1c).

obligations.title: Prepare the high-risk-system requirements and relevant sectoral conformity route, accounting for the 2 August 2028 application date.

finding.title: The intended purpose falls within an Annex III employment area
finding.summary: Employment or worker-management purpose is established. The constituent elements of Article 6(3) must still be tested before a final high-risk conclusion.

obligations.title: Document the Article 6(3) analysis and retain the evidence.

rules.title: Confirmed high-risk Annex III employment use

finding.title: The employment use matches the high-risk classification test
finding.summary: The use falls within Annex III point 4 and the supplied Article 6(3) facts do not remove it from high-risk classification. Chapter III Sections 1 to 3 apply to Annex III systems from 2 December 2027.

obligations.title: Prepare provider and deployer duties, registration, conformity, oversight, monitoring and evidence for application from 2 December 2027.

finding.title: The supplied facts match an Article 6(3) exception condition
finding.summary: The Annex III use is recorded as non-profiling, non-material, without significant risk, and limited to a listed task category.

obligations.title: Document the assessment before placing the system on the market or putting it into service and complete any required registration.

finding.title: The actor may acquire provider obligations
finding.summary: Putting an actor's name or trademark on an existing high-risk system, substantially modifying one, or changing a system's intended purpose so it becomes high-risk can make that actor the provider of the specific system.

obligations.title: Identify the actor, modification, system boundary and resulting provider obligations.

finding.title: People must be informed that they are interacting with AI
finding.summary: The system directly interacts with natural persons, its AI nature is not established as obvious, and the limited law-enforcement exception is not established.

obligations.title: Provide clear and timely information that the person is interacting with an AI system.

finding.title: No AI-literacy support measure is evidenced
finding.summary: The organisation uses AI but the inventory does not evidence measures supporting development of AI literacy for relevant people.

obligations.title: Define support measures based on technical knowledge, experience, education, training, context and affected people; no specific individual level must be guaranteed.
